Every figure of the run is a placeholder (doc/facts.py) and every run-dependent sentence a conditional. The literal numbers are constants of the SPEC, of the manifest and of the harness, listed under `_assumes`. Every claim follows SPEC-pattern-search.md sections 7 (contexts, strands, counts, the floor, the low-complexity note), 9 (what an answer licenses), 14.3 (placement), 21 (bounded mismatches), SPEC-labeled-traversal-core.md sections 4 (resolve), 6.1 (seed validation) and 6.6 (seed re-entry), areas.py _gen_N, _real_repeats, _near_miss_more and chance_bound, checks.py and service_by_design.json. Readability review (READ-312 to READ-319, 2026-10-16): a `purpose` slot; the conclusion leads with what held, the evidence gaps as counts and the gate consequence, the coverage paragraph groups the exceptions by family and recorded reason (the exception index and the detail blocks hold the ids and timings); the Background states the measured manifest version, gives the absence claim per route with its scope, labels the coordinate systems of the mutated resolve, and a version note collects every v5 change as not exercised by a v4 run (no legend's v4 branch names v5); N-hard and N-realrep say what a repeat's count and a 0 bp re-entry are not; `details` carries N-usecase-0005's reader title (the current run's assertion) and N-hard-0022's reading of the seed budget beside the wall; N-usecase-defect is labelled a diagnostic pin with its gate reading; every unit carries a reader-level `question`; access path replaces arm in the prose.

title: Negatives and near-misses
purpose: A user who gets no hit, a weak hit or a strange hit needs to know what the answer means. This chapter asks the three routes what they say when the query is not in the index (random or shuffled sequence), almost in it (a record's k-mer with more substitutions than allowed) or hard (homopolymers, tandem and telomeric repeats), and runs an agent's ordinary requests (16S primers, a wrong strand, a too-short pattern, identifying a read) with their failure modes. The evidence mixes I.2's kinds: negative controls whose absence is bounded, not proved; planted near misses with a known witness; and consistency between routes (N-zero's relations). Every absence here is bounded by the graph, the query and the labels searched (I.1's result units) and is no statement about biology beyond the index.

intro: This run executed manifest version {manifest_version}; [[manifest_version >= 5 ? the version note at the end of the coverage paragraph says how this version differs from version 4. | the version note at the end of the coverage paragraph says what a later version changes in this chapter.]] The chapter asks the three routes what they answer when the query is not in the index, almost in it, or hard. *What an empty answer rules out differs by route*, and none of the three is a statement about biology outside the indexed scope (I.1's result units: the three absence claims). On `/pattern` a negative is an exact 0 with a complete empty list, the absence claim of SPEC-pattern-search section 9: no retained k-mer of the index holds the pattern in the scope and on the strands searched (for a pattern longer than k, exact 0 paths under `long_search` paths). On `/resolve` it is a label supporting no k-mer of the query, which says that no record of that label carries them while other labels may, or, for a discovery, that no k-mer of the query is in the graph at all. On `/traverse` it is the seed's 400: a seed not fully present in the graph cannot start this traversal (SPEC-labeled-traversal-core section 6.1: the caller's error, never a walk), a precondition failure, not a search. A near miss is a record's k-mer with t substitutions searched with `max_mismatches` m below t (section 21): the record's contexts are out of reach at every level, where `source_absent` reads the chosen source's own contexts out of the results and so excludes that source alone, not every similar sequence of the index; the pair that keeps m of the substitutions brings them back at level m with the substitutions the answer states in the pattern's coordinates (section 21.8). Hard regions are homopolymers, short tandem repeats and telomeric repeats: on this basic graph a context is a graph k-mer at an offset, not an occurrence, and identical copies collapse into the same k-mers, so a pattern of L bases has at most 2 (k - L + 1) 4^(k - L) contexts whatever its copy number, and an exact pattern that sdust flags over its whole text carries the note `low_complexity_pattern` when its answer states no budget stop of the search (section 7.8). The use cases are an agent's: universal 16S primers as IUPAC patterns on both strands, a primer pair searched on one strand, a reverse complement searched forward, patterns below the information floor of 24 bits (section 7.8; chapter M's Background explains the floor as an admission rule) and a degenerate one just above it, a read identified by discovery and placed by its first k-mer (section 14.3), and the documented defect of this index (a peptide in its own genetic code and in the standard one was planned and is not built: N-usecase says why).

Ground truth. Random DNA and random low-degeneracy peptides are controls the records cannot certify[[manifest_version >= 5 ?: the builder states each one's chance bound (the union bound over the graph's k-mers of a uniform query, areas.py `chance_bound`) and refuses a control above `1e-4`; a shuffled window of a record (sco, ser, scem, dme) adds its composition-matched worst case |; this manifest states no chance bound for them, so their absence is likely by length and composition and never certified (the version note on the chapter page); a shuffled window of a record (sco, ser, scem, dme) keeps the record's composition]]. The near misses take 31-mers of the records of I.2 with one to five substitutions more than `max_mismatches` (at least four in the even-numbered ones, at most eight), clustered or spread, at `max_mismatches` 0 to 3, the host's cap; their pairs keep the first m substitutions. The mutated resolves substitute every 15 bases of a 200 bp window (no k-mer survives) or one base at query position 100; two coordinate systems meet here: the substitution is a base position of the query, counted from 0, while a support run is an interval of k-mer start positions, half-open, over the 170 k-mers of a 200 bp query (starts 0 to 169, the last being 200 - k), so the 31 k-mers starting at 70 to 100 contain the substituted base and break the runs, and the column covers [0, 70) and [101, 170), the k-mers starting at 0 to 69 and at 101 to 169; no run ends at 200 because no k-mer starts there[[manifest_version >= 5 ?, and the header's runs are stated exactly for a whole record]]. The real repeats are the longest perfect tandem repeat of period 1 to 6 and at least 40 bp in each record that has one (sco, pae, mge, sce, spo, cal, scem, tth, pfa, ath, hsa, hsv1), found in the fetched sequence; the 16S primer sites are found by brute force on both strands of the E. coli record. Every /pattern request names `time_budget_ms` [[manifest_version >= 6 ? 110,000 | 60,000]] and, but for the twelve low-complexity patterns of N-hard under `max_contexts` 100, `max_contexts` 10,000 as the service sends them, so a 503 deadline is allowed under load and reads inconclusive, and a list cut by time leaves a near miss inconclusive; the telomeric walk names a 5,000 ms budget and `max_extension_bp` 200 (what that budget covers: I.2's budget table and the detail block of N-hard-0022).

Via MCP the chapter's /pattern requests are the `pattern_search` tool (a search in the service's queue; the host's 503 deadline ends the task and comes back as 502 `search_failed`, the answer-triggered case `pattern.deadline_ends_task`), its resolves the `traverse_resolve` job (`resolve.job_path`), its seeds the traversal tool; the tool's strand words `plus` and `minus` are mapped to the host's `forward` and `reverse` before the request (`pattern.strands_vocabulary`), and the service's answer does not echo an entry's `strands`, so that field is not exposed there. Appendix B names each case with the service's code and text.

N-negative.title: negatives
N-negative.prose: Queries with nothing in the index, one per route and kind. Random DNA of 31, 40, 60, 100 and 200 bp on `/pattern`: exact 0 contexts for the 31-mer, exact 0 paths with `long_search` paths above k, and the empty list complete (`absent`): an absence over the index's retained k-mers in the scope and on the strands searched, nothing more. The shuffled 60 bp of a record (sco, ser, scem, dme), in pairs: exact 0 paths on `/pattern` and, under the record's own column on `/resolve`, `kmers_supported` 0 (`resolve_runs` with kmers 0: the label listed, supporting nothing; whether the shuffle's k-mers are in the graph through other records is not asked). Random 100 and 200 bp on `/resolve` as a discovery with `max_labels` 20: `graph_runs` empty and no label (`resolve_absent`). The same random sequences as seeds on `/traverse` with 100 bp of extension: the seed's 400 with the host's text, the seed not fully present in the graph and its graph runs stated (SPEC-labeled-traversal-core section 6.1), never a walk and never a search of anything. A random peptide of [[manifest_version >= 5 ? 12, 20 and 30 | 10, 20 and 30]] residues drawn from the low-degeneracy residues (M, W, C, F, Y, H, Q, N, K, D, E) under the standard code: exact 0 (contexts for a peptide of at most k bases, paths above it)[[manifest_version >= 5 ?; 12 residues is the shortest at which the chance bound stays below the builder's limit]]. [[manifest_version >= 5 ? Each control's chance bound is in its truth. | This manifest states no chance bound for a control (the version note on the chapter page).]] [[n_footnoted ? In this run {n_footnoted:word} of the {n_tests} tests did not pass on every access path ({footnoted_ids}): the coverage paragraph on the chapter page says why, and the detail blocks follow the tables. | In this run every test passed on every access path it was exercised on.]]
N-negative.claim: a random or shuffled query answers an exact 0 with a complete empty list on /pattern, no supported k-mer or nothing to discover on /resolve, and the seed's 400 on /traverse

N-nearmiss.title: near-misses
N-nearmiss.prose: A 31-mer of a record with t substitutions, t above `max_mismatches` m, searched in `partial`: the record's contexts are out of reach at every level (`source_absent`, which needs the complete list: a list cut by time or withheld reads inconclusive, nothing being assumed about the other contexts; the check excludes the chosen source, not every similar sequence); its pair keeps m of the substitutions, so the record's contexts come back at level m with exactly those substitutions in the pattern's coordinates (`contains_source_context` with `level` and `substitutions`, SPEC-pattern-search section 21.8). Sixteen variants over the records of I.2 (bsu, cje, mja, cal, hsa, cel, eco, sau, ser, spo, ath, dmem, hiv1, pae, mpn, sce), m from 0 to 3, clustered or spread, with twelve pairs (m above 0). Four decapeptides of the protein set with two to four substituted residues at `max_mismatches` 1: out of reach on the protein's strand (timing class slow in the manifest). The mutated seeds, grouped: 200 bp of pae, spo and cel with a substitution every 15 bases resolved under the column, no k-mer of the record surviving (`resolve_runs` with `max_kmers` 0, since every k-mer holds a substitution); one substitution at query base 100, the column covering the k-mer start intervals [0, 70) and [101, 170) on both sides of the 31 broken k-mers (the Background labels the two coordinate systems; the column may hold the variant in another record, so it is asked to cover, not to equal[[manifest_version >= 5 ?, and the header's runs are asked exactly where the record is whole]]); and the substituted seed under the record's header on `/traverse`, a seed refusal ([[manifest_version >= 5 ? not fully present in the graph, or no seed label supporting every k-mer where another record holds the variant | not fully present in the graph]]). Every /pattern search here is tagged machine-dependent (the time budget may cut its list or answer 503); the mutated resolves and seeds are not. [[n_footnoted ? In this run {n_footnoted:word} of the {n_tests} tests did not pass on every access path ({footnoted_ids}): the coverage paragraph on the chapter page counts their time limitations and 503 deadlines, and their detail blocks follow the units' tables[[n_clean ?; the {n_clean:word} other{n_clean:s} passed on every access path exercised]]. | In this run every test passed on every access path it was exercised on.]] [[n_mcp_by_design ? Via MCP {n_mcp_by_design} pair{n_mcp_by_design:s} stand{n_mcp_by_design:v} by design, the host's deadline relayed as 502 `search_failed` (see B)[[!mcp_by_design_all_verified ?, {n_mcp_by_design_unverified} unverified ({n_mcp_by_design_unverified_direct} where no direct access path answered the 503, {n_mcp_by_design_unverified_other_repeat} where the other repeat's 200 has no direct 200 to compare with)]].]]
N-nearmiss.claim: a record's k-mer with more substitutions than max_mismatches is out of reach, and the pair with exactly m is back at level m with its substitutions stated

N-nearmiss2.title: more near-misses
N-nearmiss2.prose: The same question at another length and on the other strand, on low-carrier records: a 25-mer of cal with three spread substitutions at `max_mismatches` 1, out of reach; the reverse complement of a mja 31-mer with four substitutions at `max_mismatches` 2, the `-` source out of reach (the record's contexts are `-` contexts of the pattern); and its pair with one substitution at `max_mismatches` 1, the `-` source back at level 1 with the substitutions in the pattern's coordinates (section 21.8: the substitutions of a `-` context are stated on the pattern, not on the record). [[n_footnoted ? In this run {n_footnoted:word} of the {n_tests:word} tests did not pass on every access path ({footnoted_ids}): the coverage paragraph on the chapter page says why, and the detail blocks follow the tables. | In this run every test passed on every access path it was exercised on.]]
N-nearmiss2.claim: near misses hold at 25 bp and on the '-' strand, the pair's substitutions stated in the pattern's coordinates

N-hard.title: hard regions
N-hard.prose: Low-complexity patterns whose contexts are few by construction and whose note the SPEC fixes: `A^31`, `(AT)^15A`, `(CAG)^10`, `(CA)^12C` and the telomeric `(TTAGGG)^5` and `(CCCTAA)^5`, each in `partial` with `max_contexts` 100 (count exact, at least 1 and at most 2 (k - L + 1) 4^(k - L): a context is a graph k-mer at an offset, so a homopolymer of k bases has at most two) and in `all_or_count` with `max_contexts` 100 (complete and never withheld where the bound is within 100; `(CA)^12C`, whose bound exceeds it, may be withheld as `count_above_threshold`), the note `low_complexity_pattern` exactly where the host's sdust (T 20, W 64) flags the pattern (`low_complexity_note`: present for the homopolymer and the dinucleotide and trinucleotide repeats, absent for the telomeric ones, SPEC-pattern-search section 7.8); above k, `A^40` and `(AT)^16` as paths in `partial` (exact paths, at least 1) and the long `A^80`, `(TTAGGG)^15` and `(CAG)^30` with `max_paths` 100 and `max_anchors` 1,000, where a stated stop or cut is allowed and the note is judged as the stop allows (a budget stop leaves it out: inconclusive where it was expected). Then repeats of the records: a 31-mer of a 2-copy repeat of eco and of a 6-copy repeat of bsu counted (exact, at least 1), the repeat window resolved under the column (full), and the telomeric seed `(TTAGGG)^10` under the human column with 200 bp of extension and a 5,000 ms budget: a 200 with the walk's stated outcome (complete or partial) or the seed's 400 if the human column lacks it, and on a 200 each traversal arm's first step into the next copy blocked as `rejoined_seed` at 0 bp (`blocked_event`: the period closes a cycle inside the seed, SPEC-labeled-traversal-core section 6.6; the depth-0 level is processed whatever the budget, so no stop hides it)[[manifest_version >= 5 ?; a warm-up resolve of the seed under the human column runs right before it (chapter R, R-warm)]]. *What these tests do not measure.* On this basic graph identical copies of a repeat collapse into the same k-mers, so a context count of a repeat says how many distinct (k-mer, offset) pairs hold the pattern, never how many genomic copies there are: a count of two is not two copies, and a count within the bound is compatible with any copy number; the tests validate context counts, support and a safe termination, not copy number. Likewise `rejoined_seed` at 0 bp is the walk's cycle guard: the first step out of the seed lands on sequence the walk has already used, so the walk extends by 0 bp beyond the seed before re-entering it; it measures no repeat length. [[n_footnoted ? In this run {n_footnoted:word} of the {n_tests} tests did not pass on every access path ({footnoted_ids}): the coverage paragraph on the chapter page says why, and the detail blocks follow the tables. | In this run every test passed on every access path it was exercised on.]]
N-hard.claim: low-complexity patterns are counted exactly within their bound with the note as sdust says, multi-copy repeats are counted (contexts, not copies) and resolved, and a telomeric seed re-enters itself at 0 bp

N-realrep.title: real repeats
N-realrep.prose: The longest perfect tandem repeat (period 1 to 6, at least 40 bp) of each record that has one, grouped by route. On `/pattern` a 31-mer inside it: every context of the record returned (`contains_source_context`), a count exact and at least the record's own distinct contexts (`count_relation`), the note stated or absent as sdust flags the 31-mer (`low_complexity_note`); the count is of distinct graph k-mers at offsets, into which the repeat's copies collapse, not of copies (N-hard says why). On `/resolve`, where the repeat is at least 60 bp, 60 bp of it under the record's column: full (`resolve_runs`), every k-mer carried although the repeat's k-mers recur. On `/traverse`, for the first two records with a whole-record header (sco, pae), a 40 bp seed inside the repeat walked under the record's header with 200 bp of extension: the walk follows the record to where it re-enters its own edges, branches or ends (`walk_in_record` with the record as the only label), a termination guard of the walk, not a measurement of the repeat's length or copy number[[manifest_version >= 5 ?, and where the period is at most 9 (40 - k, so that a seed k-mer recurs one period on inside the seed) each traversal arm's first step into the next copy is blocked as `rejoined_seed` at 0 bp (`blocked_event`)]]. [[n_footnoted ? In this run {n_footnoted:word} of the {n_tests} tests did not pass on every access path ({footnoted_ids}): the coverage paragraph on the chapter page says why, and the detail blocks follow the tables. | In this run every test passed on every access path it was exercised on.]]
N-realrep.claim: a real tandem repeat of a record is counted with its contexts and note, resolved fully under its column, and walked to its re-entry

N-usecase.title: use cases
N-usecase.prose: An agent's ordinary requests with their failure modes. The four universal 16S primers (`27F`, `1492R`, `515F`, `806R`) as IUPAC patterns in mode count on both strands: exact, at least the E. coli record's own site contexts (found by brute force on both strands). Independent primer searches test no amplicon: not the pair's orientation, their spacing or a successful amplification, only what each primer matches on the strands asked. The strand mistakes: the pair `515F` and `806R` with `strands` forward, [[manifest_version >= 5 ? both entries searched on `+` only and both counted (`entry_fields`, `count_relation`; the reverse primer's forward count is the records holding the gene on the other strand) | only the first entry's `strands` field is checked (`+` only; `entry_fields`): the second primer's strands and both counts are asserted by no check of this manifest]], and the reverse complement of a 25 bp eco window searched forward only, the record's k-mers not found (`source_absent` on `+`: this basic graph holds the records' forward strands). The floor: 10 bp (20 bits) and 20 N with 11 bases (22 bits) are refused in their slot with `information_below_floor` and the host's exact text (`pattern_slot_error`, section 7.8; chapter M's Background explains the floor as an admission rule); 12 N with 13 bases (26 bits) is admitted, and the 13 bases at every offset make it costly (count at least 1, exact or at least; a 503 deadline allowed). Identifying a read: 150 bp of mge and of hsa discovered under `max_labels` 100 names the record's taxid (`resolve_discover_contains`), and its first 31 bp under `any(A)` with `predicate_only` is placed at the window's coordinates and strand in its record (`source_placement`, section 14.3). The builder's pair of a mitochondrial peptide in its own table and in table 1 needs a decapeptide of the protein set that reads differently in table 1 and sits in a fetched record; none does in this manifest, so the unit holds no such pair ([[manifest_version >= 5 ? the skipped list states it | this manifest leaves it unstated: the version note on the chapter page]]). The documented defect: the rbcL 31-mer of `NC_000932.1` is in the graph (`graph_runs` [[0, 1]]) but its header supports none of it (`resolve_runs` with kmers 0); the expectation pins the defect of 2026-10-09, so the test documents it and fails once the index is repaired (N-usecase-defect). [[n_footnoted ? In this run {n_footnoted:word} of the {n_tests} tests did not pass on every access path ({footnoted_ids}): the coverage paragraph on the chapter page says why, and the detail blocks follow the tables. | In this run every test passed on every access path it was exercised on.]] [[x[N-usecase-0005][mcp][standing] = inconclusive ? Via MCP the forward-only pair's `strands` field is not in the tool's answer (`pattern.strands_vocabulary`, see B), so that entry check is not exposed there.]]
N-usecase.claim: the primers are counted on both strands, a forward-only search finds what the record holds on +, the floor refuses with the host's text and admits just above it, a read is identified and placed, and the index defect is as documented

N-zero.title: zero equals absent
N-zero.prose: The two routes agree on absence: a random 31-mer, a random 60 bp, a 31-mer of sco, 60 bp of cal and a 31-mer of sso with one substitution at position 15 (present or not: the routes must agree), each searched forward only on `/pattern` and resolved on `/resolve`, with the relation `zero_equals_absent` on each pair: the count (contexts, or paths above k) is exact 0 on `/pattern` if and only if some k-mer is absent from the graph on `/resolve` (`graph_runs` shorter than the query). The agreement is between two readings of the same graph, not an absence from any genome: exact 0 means that no retained k-mer holds the pattern on the strand searched, and a shortened `graph_runs` that some k-mer of the query is in no record of the index. The tests themselves ask only a 200 with consistent counts; the claim is the relations'. [[n_relations ? Of the {n_relations:word} relations, {relations_text}.]] [[n_footnoted ? In this run {n_footnoted:word} of the {n_tests} tests did not pass on every access path ({footnoted_ids}): the coverage paragraph on the chapter page says why, and the detail blocks follow the tables. | In this run every test passed on every access path it was exercised on.]]
N-zero.claim: exact 0 on /pattern holds exactly when a k-mer is absent on /resolve (relations zero_equals_absent)

N-negative-random.property: Random DNA of 31 to 200 bp on /pattern: exact 0 (contexts at k, paths above it) with a complete empty list.
N-negative-random.question: Does random DNA answer an exact 0 with a complete empty list on /pattern (an absence over the index's retained k-mers in the scope searched)?

N-negative-shuffled.property: A shuffled 60 bp window of a record: exact 0 paths on /pattern, and under the record's column on /resolve no k-mer supported.
N-negative-shuffled.question: Does a shuffled window answer exact 0 paths on /pattern and, under its record's column on /resolve, no supported k-mer?

N-negative-discover.property: Random 100 and 200 bp on /resolve as a discovery: no k-mer in the graph, nothing to discover.
N-negative-discover.question: Does a random discovery on /resolve find no k-mer in the graph and nothing to discover?

N-negative-seed.property: A random 100 or 200 bp seed on /traverse: the seed's 400 (not fully present in the graph, its graph runs stated), never a walk.
N-negative-seed.question: Is a random seed refused by /traverse with its graph runs stated, never walked?

N-negative-peptide.property: A random peptide of low-degeneracy residues under the standard code: exact 0 (contexts at most k bases, paths above it).
N-negative-peptide.note: [[manifest_version >= 5 ? The shortest is 12 residues (36 bases, the shortest whose chance bound stays below the builder's limit); 20 and 30 residues complete the set. | The shortest is 10 residues; 20 and 30 residues complete the set (a later manifest raises the shortest to 12: the version note on the chapter page).]]
N-negative-peptide.question: Does a random low-degeneracy peptide answer exact 0 under the standard code?

N-nearmiss-pairs.property: A 31-mer with t substitutions above max_mismatches m puts the record's contexts out of reach at every level (a complete list needed); the pair with exactly m brings them back at level m with the substitutions stated.
N-nearmiss-pairs.question: Is a record's k-mer with more substitutions than allowed absent from every level of a complete list, and does the pair with exactly m bring it back at level m with its substitutions stated?

N-nearmiss-peptide.property: A decapeptide with two to four substituted residues at max_mismatches 1: the record's contexts out of reach on the protein's strand.
N-nearmiss-peptide.question: Is a decapeptide with two to four substituted residues out of reach at max_mismatches 1?

N-nearmiss-mutated.property: A substitution every 15 bases of 200 bp leaves no k-mer of the record under its column; one substitution at query base 100 breaks the runs there with both sides covered (k-mer start intervals [0, 70) and [101, 170), half-open); the mutated seed under the record's header is refused by /traverse.
N-nearmiss-mutated.question: Does a mutated 200 bp window resolve with no surviving k-mer, a single substitution break the runs with both sides covered, and the mutated seed get refused?

N-nearmiss2.property: A 25-mer with three spread substitutions and the reverse complement of a 31-mer with four are out of reach at max_mismatches 1 and 2; the pair with one substitution is back at level 1, the '-' source's substitutions stated in the pattern's coordinates.
N-nearmiss2.question: Do near misses hold at 25 bp and on the - strand, with the pair's substitutions stated in the pattern's coordinates?

N-hard-lowcomplex.property: Low-complexity patterns: exact counts within 2 (k - L + 1) 4^(k - L), the note low_complexity_pattern exactly as sdust says; complete and never withheld within max_contexts 100; above k their paths counted, the long ones with stated stops or a cut allowed.
N-hard-lowcomplex.question: Are low-complexity patterns counted exactly within their bound, with the low_complexity_pattern note exactly as sdust says?

N-hard-repeat.property: A 31-mer of a multi-copy repeat is counted (distinct graph k-mers at offsets, not copies) and its window resolved with every k-mer carried; the telomeric seed `(TTAGGG)^10` re-enters itself at 0 bp (rejoined_seed: the walk's cycle guard, no repeat length) with its stated outcome, or is refused where the human column lacks it.
N-hard-repeat.question: Is a multi-copy repeat's k-mer counted (contexts, not copies) and its window resolved, and does the telomeric seed re-enter itself at 0 bp or get refused where the human column lacks it?
N-hard-repeat.note: The telomeric walk's 5,000 ms budget covers the walk from depth 1 on the seed's own clock, not the seed phase, the finalisation or the service's phases (I.2's budget table): its wall times may exceed it while the budget check (budget_respected) passes; the detail block of N-hard-0022, when there is one, says so beside the rows.

N-realrep.property: Real tandem repeats of the records: on /pattern the record's contexts and the note as sdust says, on /resolve 60 bp of the repeat fully supported, on /traverse a 40 bp seed followed along the record to its re-entry or branch[[manifest_version >= 5 ?, the re-entry at 0 bp stated where the period allows]].
N-realrep.question: Are a record's real tandem repeats counted with their contexts and note, resolved fully under the column, and walked to the re-entry or branch?

N-usecase-primers.property: A universal 16S primer as an IUPAC pattern on both strands is counted exactly, at least the E. coli record's own site contexts.
N-usecase-primers.question: Is a universal 16S primer counted exactly on both strands, at least the E. coli record's own site contexts?

N-usecase-strand.property: A forward-only search of a primer pair reads [[manifest_version >= 5 ? its entries on + only and counts both | its first entry on + only (the second primer is asserted by no check of this manifest)]]; the reverse complement of a window searched forward does not find the record's k-mers. Neither tests an amplicon.
N-usecase-strand.question: Does a forward-only search report its entries on + only, and does a reverse complement searched forward miss the record's k-mers?

N-usecase-floor.property: Patterns of 20 and 22 information bits are refused in their slot below the floor of 24 with the host's text; 12 N with 13 bases (26 bits) is admitted and costly (a count at least 1, or a 503 deadline under load).
N-usecase-floor.question: Are patterns below the floor refused with the host's text, and is the degenerate one just above it admitted and counted (or a 503 allowed)?

N-usecase-identify.property: A 150 bp read is identified: its discovery names the record's taxid, and its first 31 bp under any(A) are placed at the window's coordinates in the record.
N-usecase-identify.question: Is a 150 bp read identified by discovery and its first k-mer placed at the window's coordinates in the record?

N-usecase-defect.property: Diagnostic pin of a known index defect, not acceptance evidence: the rbcL 31-mer of NC_000932.1 is in the graph, but its header supports none of it (the defect of 2026-10-09). A pass confirms that the defect still stands in this index; on a repaired index this test fails by design.
N-usecase-defect.question: Does the known index defect still stand (the rbcL 31-mer in the graph, its header supporting none of it)? A pass confirms the defect, not the index.
N-usecase-defect.note: How to read either outcome: a pass here is a statement about the index, never approval of it; a failure signals the repair, not a regression of the host, and calls for revising the pinned expectation with the repaired index's facts. [[gate_judged ? [[x[N-usecase-0014][gate_selected] ? The gate's policy selects this scenario (its route is one the policy selects; the scope is on the cover and in appendix F), so on a gated access path that failure would count as an observed violation until the expectation is revised. | The gate's policy does not select this scenario, so that failure would not count against the gate.]] | The deploy gate was not judged for this run (I.1), so nothing here says how that failure would count.]]

N-zero.property: exact 0 on /pattern (forward only) if and only if a k-mer is absent on /resolve, on random and record queries (relations zero_equals_absent).
N-zero.question: Is exact 0 on /pattern equivalent to a k-mer absent on /resolve, on random and record queries?

N-usecase-0005.title: [[manifest_version >= 5 ? a primer pair on the forward strand only (one primer is reverse): both entries report + and both are counted | a primer pair on the forward strand only (one primer is reverse): the first entry reports forward-only strands]]

N-hard-0022.note: The requested budget of 5,000 ms is the seed's `time_budget_ms`: it governs the walk from depth 1 on the seed's own clock and nothing else (I.2's budget table). Around it lie phases the budget does not cover: the seed phase (validating the seed and finding its graph runs), the depth-0 level, the finalisation of the answer and, via MCP, the service's submit, queue and paging; the wall column is the client's clock over all of them. A 200 whose walk stayed within its budget therefore passes `budget_respected` at a wall time above 5,000 ms, and the chapter's statement that no 200 exceeded its budget is about that contract budget, not about end-to-end latency. The host also bounds the whole attempt's duration (the load, the seeds' budgets and a reserve, as its own text in this block states)[[x[N-hard-0022][mcp][standing] = inconclusive ?: in this run the cold MCP call reached that bound in the seed phase, before any seed was walked, so nothing the seed budget governs happened and the walk checks read not testable, inconclusive, not failed; the warm call passed. | ; when it ends the seed phase before any walk, the walk checks read not testable: inconclusive, not failed.]]
